what_happened: Dispatch's central design question (a vs b) assumed specs/state.json writes go through a single Write|Edit-tool boundary; research found the write path is heterogeneous (state-write.sh via Bash for some surfaces, raw jq via Bash for meta-builder-agent and skill-fix-it) so a Write|Edit-matched PreToolUse hook as literally described in option (a) would never fire. Resolved by ruling a two-layer design anchored at scripts/state-write.sh instead.

All nine tasks named as blocking in the dispatch's cost calculus (263,280,281,282,307 for option a; 44,300,302,308,309 for option b), plus this task's own four declared dependencies (165,282,300,344), are now completed or abandoned -- the cost calculus is moot and the decision rests entirely on the uniformity-vs-blocking-depth grounds already named.

Inherited deliverable name audit-open-tasks.sh (declared in file_scope) contradicts the owner-widened open-union-closed contract. Ruled at planning time (plan D1) as scripts/audit-task-proposals.sh; the declared file_scope entry for audit-open-tasks.sh is superseded and must not be created.

Research left commands/errors.md's write mechanism unverified. Planning verified it: grep -c state-write returns 0 AND it has no next_project_number/active_projects write site at all (one read-only jq query). So the state-write.sh migration set stays at two files (meta-builder-agent.md, skill-fix-it/SKILL.md) and errors.md needs only audit-call wiring. Captured as Phase 8's Scope Hypothesis.

Both reads the new matcher needs already have single-source libraries: lib/file-scope-overlap.sh (overlap predicate, two consumption shapes) and lib/project-number-inuse.sh (already unions live active_projects with archive completed/archived/abandoned and tolerates that archive's 24 measured cross-array duplicate numbers). No new corpus-union code is needed, and validate-artifact.sh passed the plan with 0 warnings first try.
